newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma enacts law for licensing insurance business.
newsitem.headline: Burma enacts law for licensing insurance business.

text.p: The ministry of finance and revenue has enacted "Insurance Business Rules" to pave the way for licensing private local and foreign companies to operate insurance businesses in Burma.

Ba Tun, managing director of state-owned Myanmar Insurance, said the rules, enacted last week, would initially allow Burmese incorporated companies to open six categories of insurance business including life, fire, comprehensive motor vehicle, cash-in-transit, cash-in-safe, and fidelity insurance.
The official said foreign firms would later be licensed to form insurance joint ventures or launch their own businesses in Burma. "They will be allowed when necessary," he said.
Foreign firms are currently permitted to open only representative offices in Burma. They include Japan's Mitsui Marine and Fire Insurance Co Ltd and Yasuda Fire and Marine Insurance Co Ltd.
Yasuda last month also reached a preliminary agreement to form an insurance joint venture with Myanmar Insurance.

Burma had 74 insurance companies in the early 1960s when armed forces chief General Ne Win took power through a military coup and ruled the country with an iron hand. He resigned in 1988. The companies were closed during the country's 26 years of socialism.
